items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: I think Bushrell is right that it was quite legitimate, the sounding.

ctx.x: Well, you ought to sit down and listen to it through, you know, to hear the difference in what was going on in New York. It's interesting to hear the variations in style there.

So in that sense, I think Bushrell is right that it was quite legitimate, the sounding. That could be just a prejudice, of course, we have too because we were sold so much on New Orleans music. But at least the evidence on the early records certainly points that way, the originality down here. That's a legitimate sound up there.

There's another, we were mentioning Louie just a minute ago. There is a notion that those early musicians who left New Orleans early, like King Oliver, Louie, that New Orleans was a very communal organization. The musicians stuck together and that was reflected in the style of music as well. And that those that left tended not to fit into the communal pattern of living. And that Louie might have been, you know, couldn't have played in an ensemble band or wasn't a communal soul.
